behavior: Both the authenticated endpoint and core require the loaded viewer identity; mismatches stop before database access.
Caller-scoped document lookup plus canonical student/document read authority precede existing-review retrieval. Existing viewers do not need editing access to read an available review.
A confirmed absent review alone may proceed to initialization, with canonical editing authority and partner-only exclusion. Read errors and malformed replies stop without insertion.
Only one empty pending twelve-section review is inserted with the authenticated creator; complete identity, state, sections and empty generated/meta fields are verified before return.
Current read authority is checked again before returning either an existing or newly initialized review.
No automatic retry, upsert or conflict fallback. Lost/concurrent insertion outcomes require refresh; a committed empty row may already exist.
The browser sends the originating viewer, suppresses departed results/errors and shows a fixed user-friendly load error without private transport text.
limitations: Independent reads and insert do not provide transaction-held authorization serialization; caller RLS and database guards remain necessary.
No hosted permission/removal/concurrent-client acceptance is claimed. No schema, grants or existing private access exceptions were changed.
Existing SQL/native evidence is retained only for unchanged SQL; no fresh native database replay is claimed.
Uncertain initialization does not certify rollback. It may leave one valid empty review; users must refresh instead of blindly resubmitting.
No generation, provider call, quota admission, document byte mutation or cleanup is performed by initialization.
